surprises.head: Vancouver got the good looks
surprises.body: Vancouver’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.4% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

story.head: The Red Wings cruise past the Canucks
paras: Emmitt Finnie scored early in the first and again less than three minutes later to put the Red Wings up 2-0. Lucas Raymond made it 3-0 on the power play with just under a minute left in the period. J.T. Compher stretched the lead to 4-0 early in the second, but Paul Cotter got the Canucks on the board early in the third. Viktor Arvidsson extended the lead to 5-1, 42 seconds later. Cole Reinhardt made his Canucks debut, after two seasons with the Panthers, and picked up an assist. Two players had three-point nights: Arvidsson with a goal and two assists, and Finnie with two goals and an assist.

The chances were closer than the score. Daniil Tarasov made 25 saves for the Red Wings, and Leevi Meriläinen allowed five goals on 26 shots. The Wings improved to 9-12-3 and climbed off the bottom of the Atlantic to seventh, while the Canucks fell to 6-20-1, still last in the NHL.

items.text: The Red Wings scored on the power play for the first time since Nov 3, after going 0-for-10 over seven games.
Brock Boeser’s eleven-game point streak ended.
Lucas Raymond extended his point streak against Vancouver to six games.
The Red Wings have beaten the Canucks five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
